newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt retries suspected militants after acquittal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt retries suspected militants after acquittal.

text.p: A Cairo state security court has started a retrial of five suspected Moslem militants who were acquitted by another court of charges that they killed a policeman and wounded another, court sources said on Wednesday.
A state security court in southern Egypt in 1995 found the men innocent of the charges but the prosecutor's office challenged its verdict.
The five men have been held in prison since their first trial at the orders of the interior ministry.
Defendants have no right of appeal at state security courts, where the maximum sentence is death.
They may petition for mercy from the prime minister in his capacity as deputy military governor. But the prosecutor's office can challenge sentences passed by the state security courts.
The 1995 verdict was based on the inconsistency between witness statements and investigation reports, sources said.
Egypt is trying more than 150 suspected militants in several courts in what analysts see as the final blow by the government in its fight against Moslem militant groups.
Moslem militants have been fighting the government since 1992 to establish a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in the conflict.
